plain_english: Now we declare the circle of shakti means for supreme self-knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: atha śāktamupāyamaṇḍalaṃ kathayāmaḥ paramātmasaṃvide

plain_english: In that supreme lordly nature, one desiring entry into distinction should refine it directly.
sanskrit_cite: anantarāhnikokte@sminsvabhāve pārameśvare pravivikṣurvikalpasya kuryātsaṃskāramañjasā

plain_english: Refined distinction produces a self-refined distinction equal to itself, and that produces another similar one.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpaḥ saṃskṛtaḥ sūte vikalpaṃ svātmasaṃskṛtam svatulyaṃ so@pi so@pyanyaṃ so@pyanyaṃ sadṛśātmakam

plain_english: In four distinctions, refinement gradually moves from unclear to becoming clear and fully clear-natured.
sanskrit_cite: caturṣveva vikalpeṣu yaḥ saṃskāraḥ kramādasau asphuṭaḥ sphuṭatābhāvī prasphuṭansphuṭitātmakaḥ

plain_english: Then it becomes clearer until the clearest; even from the unclear beginning, difference remains between stages.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sphuṭataro yāvadante sphuṭatamo bhavet asphuṭādau vikalpe ca bhedo@pyastyāntarālikaḥ

plain_english: Then consciousness, filled with the clearest nobility of form, approaches pure non-distinct nature.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ sphuṭatamodāratādrūpyaparivṛṃhitā saṃvidabhyeti vimalāmavikalpasvarūpatām

plain_english: Therefore, for those reflecting again and again, the clear selfhood of that consciousness-natured radiance arises.
sanskrit_cite: ataśca bhairavīyaṃ yattejaḥ saṃvitsvabhāvakam bhūyo bhūyo vimṛśatāṃ jāyate tatsphuṭātmatā

plain_english: But how can consciousness, supreme knower made of reflection, reflect by itself in such creation without becoming inert?
sanskrit_cite: nanu saṃvitparāmraṣṭrī parāmarśamayī svataḥ parāmṛśyā kathaṃ tāthārūpyasṛṣṭau tu sā jaḍā

plain_english: It is said that self-consciousness is full by nature alone; nothing is to be removed or added, as said before.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate svātmasaṃvittiḥ svabhāvādeva nirbharā nāsyāmapāsyaṃ nādheyaṃ kiṃcidityuditaṃ purā

plain_english: But the supreme lord, pure through difficult doing and free will, is skilled in the play of concealing himself.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tu durghaṭakāritvātsvācchandyānnirmalādasau svātmapracchādanakrīḍāpaṇḍitaḥ parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: Even when his own form is uncovered, the lord's self-concealment is maya, because difference occurs throughout the world.
sanskrit_cite: anāvṛtte svarūpe@pi yadātmācchādanaṃ vibhoḥ saiva māyā yato bheda etāvānviśvavṛttikaḥ

plain_english: Such appearance of the great lord is called duality; by removing that duality, this is called reflection.
sanskrit_cite: tathābhāsanamevāsya dvaitamuktaṃ maheśituḥ taddvayāpāsanenāyaṃ parāmarśo@bhidhīyate

plain_english: The wise cut the root of this hard-to-split tree with the axe of true logic; this is certain.
sanskrit_cite: durbhedapādapasyāsya mūlaṃ kṛntanti kovidāḥ dhārārūḍhena sattarkakuṭhāreṇeti niścayaḥ

plain_english: The wise call that meditation all-desire-milking; it clarifies things and removes even what rests in the mind.
sanskrit_cite: tāmenāṃ bhāvanāmāhuḥ sarvakāmadughāṃ budhāḥ sphuṭayedvastu yāpetaṃ manosthapadādapi

plain_english: In the prior scripture logic is stated to be the best limb of yoga, and effort is praised for considering what should be rejected.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaśāstre tatproktaṃ tarko yogāṅgamuttamam heyādyālocanāttasmāttatra yatnaḥ praśasyate

plain_english: When the mind is steadied on the path, even desire for objects impels it; by that it should be led until the diseaseless state.
sanskrit_cite: mārge cetaḥ sthirībhūtaṃ heye@pi viṣayecchayā prerya tena nayettāvadyāvatpadamanāmayam

plain_english: The path here is a means of liberation, but that path taught elsewhere is rejectable because desire pervades and binds what is joined with necessity.
sanskrit_cite: mārgo@tra mokṣopāyaḥ sa heyaḥ śāstrāntaroditaḥ viṣiṇoti nibadhnāti yecchā niyatisaṃgatam

plain_english: The principle of attachment, as stated by that, makes one attached there, just as seeing royal enjoyment, unseen obstruction, leads to attachment.
sanskrit_cite: rāgatattvaṃ tayoktaṃ yat tena tatrānurajyate yathā sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ dṛṣṭvādṛṣṭvāthabādhame

plain_english: One may be attached in enjoyment, even in liberation like the evil-minded; that portion is called nature, and this is clearly said.
sanskrit_cite: bhoge rajyeta durbuddhistadvanmokṣe@pi rāgataḥ sa evāṃśaka ityuktaḥ svabhāvākhyaḥ sa tu sphuṭam

plain_english: The wise say that what is called an accomplishment limb is an obstacle to liberation, even for those who know the greatness of Shiva's teaching.
sanskrit_cite: siddhyaṅgamiti mokṣāya pratyūha iti kovidāḥ śivaśāsanamāhātmyaṃ vidannapyata eva hi

plain_english: A fool may be attached in Vaishnava teachings, colored by attachment, because that is his divine power called Vama.
sanskrit_cite: vaiṣṇavādhyeṣu rajyeta mūḍho rāgeṇa rañjitaḥ yatastāvati sā tasya vāmākhyā śaktiraiśvarī

plain_english: Some foolish ones are seen blaming royal enjoyment, and this expands from Pañcaratra, Brahma, and Buddhist traditions.
sanskrit_cite: pāñcarātrikavairiñcasaugatādervijṛmbhate dṛṣṭāḥ sāmrājyasaṃbhogaṃ nindantaḥ ke@pi vāliśāḥ

plain_english: Not from contentment, but from desire proceeding in their own enjoyments, minds become intent on blaming Bhairava possession.
sanskrit_cite: na tu saṃtoṣataḥ sveṣu bhogeṣvāśīḥpravartanāt evaṃcidbhairavāveśanindātatparamānasāḥ

plain_english: They become fallen by very terrible powers; therefore, even knowers in other teachings should know the greatness of the Shaiva teaching.
sanskrit_cite: bhavantyatisughorābhiḥ śaktibhiḥ pātitā yataḥ tena śāṃbhavamāhātmyaṃ jānanyaḥ śāsanāntare

plain_english: Having been reassured, one should not cross from the great ocean of difference; this is clearly stated in the Śrīkāmikā and in the section on bonds.
sanskrit_cite: āśvasto nottarītavyaṃ tena bhedamahārṇavāt śrīkāmikāyāṃ proktaṃ ca pāśaprakaraṇe sphuṭam

plain_english: Those wise seers who know Veda, Sāṃkhya, and Purāṇas, devoted to Pāñcarātra, and devoted to other scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: vedasāṃkhyapurāṇajñāḥ pāñcarātraparāyaṇāḥ ye kecidṛṣayo dhīrāḥ śāstrāntaraparāyaṇāḥ

plain_english: All Buddhists, Arhats, and others are colored by attachment to knowledge; because they are bound by the Māyā bond, they do not obtain Śiva initiation.
sanskrit_cite: bauddhārhatādyāḥ sarve te vidyārāgeṇa rañjitāḥ māyāpāśena baddhatvācchivadīkṣāṃ na vindate

plain_english: By the word rāga is stated the rāga principle as regulator in Māyā; and that regulates him in that scripture.
sanskrit_cite: rāgaśabdena ca proktaṃ rāgatattvaṃ niyāmakam māyīye tacca taṃ tasmiñchāstre niyamayediti

plain_english: Even the liberation of Vaiṣṇavas and others is imagined by their own resolve: union with higher nature, or bliss-form.
sanskrit_cite: mokṣo@pi vaiṣṇavāderyaḥ svasaṃkalpena bhāvitaḥ paraprakṛtisāyujyaṃ yadvāpyānandarūpatā

plain_english: Or only purified mind, or lamp-like cessation of continuum; that is composed of dissolution of knowable and unknowable self into kalā.
sanskrit_cite: viśuddhacittamātraṃ vā dīpavatsaṃtatikṣayaḥ sa savedyāpavedyātmapralayākalatāmayaḥ

plain_english: Having attained it, for a long time, consumed by that enjoyment; at the end of dissolution of that principle, then one goes to a higher creation.
sanskrit_cite: taṃ prāpyāpi ciraṃ kālaṃ tadgogābhogabhuktataḥ tattattvapralayānte tu tadūrdhvāṃ sṛṣṭimāgataḥ

plain_english: It becomes mantra by awakening from Ananteśa's creation; we will explain this ahead; let that be for now here.
sanskrit_cite: mantratvameti saṃbodhādananteśena kalpitāt etaccāgre taniṣyāma ityāstāṃ tāvadatra tat

plain_english: He who is mocked by doctrines fabricated by ignorant people, rooted in false guru, is colored by the Māyā bond.
sanskrit_cite: tenājñajanatāklṛptapravādairyo viḍambitaḥ asadgurau rūḍhacitsa māyāpāśena rañjitaḥ

plain_english: He too, by union of right reasoning, is led toward the true guru; right reasoning is pure knowledge, and that is the will of the supreme lord.
sanskrit_cite: so@pi sattarkayogena nīyate sadguruṃ prati sattarkaḥ śuddhavidyaiva sā cecchā parameśituḥ

plain_english: In the Śrīpūrva scripture it is said by him: desiring, by Śiva's will, for accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation, one is led toward the true guru.
sanskrit_cite: śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ sa yiyāsuḥ śivecchayā bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati

plain_english: But grace there proceeds gradually, for one who, abiding in the true guru or in another scripture, has taken the right path.
sanskrit_cite: śaktipātastu tatraiṣa kramikaḥ saṃpravartate sthitvā yo@sadgurau śāstrāntare vā satpathaṃ śritaḥ

plain_english: Here, in the being guided by guru and scripture, the variety of descent of power is distinguished beforehand.
sanskrit_cite: guruśāstragate sattve@sattve cātra vibhedakam śaktipātasya vaicitryaṃ purastātpravivicyate

plain_english: As said in the Svacchanda scripture, māyā deludes all teachers, even in liberation, through desire for liberation.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre tat vaiṣṇavādyānpravādinaḥ sarvānbhramayate māyā sāmokṣe moKṣalipsayā

plain_english: But one rooted there, skilled in reflection, is purified by descent of power through the glory of pure knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: yastu rūḍho@pi tatrodyatparāmarśaviśāradaḥ sa śuddhavidyāmāhātmyācchaktipātapavitritaḥ

plain_english: He ascends the true path free from obstacles, and his reasoning proceeds from himself.
sanskrit_cite: ārohatyeva sanmārgaṃ pratyūhaparivarjitaḥ sa tāvatkasyacittarkaḥ svata eva pravartate

plain_english: This innate, self-evident knowledge is declared in scripture; even in the Kiraṇa it is said to come from guru, scripture, and self.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca sāṃsiddhikaḥ śāstre proktaḥ svapratyayātmakaḥ kiraṇāyāṃ yadapyuktaṃ gurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ

plain_english: There, increasingly primary means are the former means; one whose true reasoning arises from himself is entitled everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: tatrottarottaraṃ mukhyaṃ pūrvapūrva upāyakaḥ yasya svato@yaṃ sattarkaḥ sarvatraivādhikāravān

plain_english: Consecrated and initiated by the goddesses of self-knowledge, he alone is proclaimed chief among all teachers.
sanskrit_cite: abhiṣiktaḥ svasaṃvittidevībhirdīkṣitaśca saḥ sa eva sarvācāryāṇāṃ madhye mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ

plain_english: In his presence, not in others, is authority; he understands all scripture meaning from true reasoning alone.
sanskrit_cite: tatsaṃnidhāne nānyeṣu kalpiteṣvadhikāritā sa samastaṃ ca śāstrārthaṃ sattarkādeva manyate

plain_english: Pure knowledge is truth; if it does not illuminate, then his sudden knowing of all scripture meaning arises.
sanskrit_cite: śuddhavidyā hi tannāsti satyaṃ yadyanna bhāsayet sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate

plain_english: Thus in the previous sacred statement, from the word sudden, the reason not famous in the world is said to be why.
sanskrit_cite: iti śrīpūvavākye tad+akasmāditi-śabdataḥ lokāprasiddho yo hetuḥ so@kasmāditi kathyate

plain_english: This is the expansion of pure knowledge of the supreme lord; its teachings are many, both without foundation and with foundation.
sanskrit_cite: sa caiṣa parameśānaśuddhavidyāvijṛmbhatam asya bhodāśca bahavo nirbhittiḥ sahabhittikaḥ

plain_english: He, gone to all parts, is established in primary and secondary parts: foundation, dependence on others, supreme wisdom, and its making.
sanskrit_cite: sarvago@ṃśagataḥ so@pi mukhyāmukhyāṃśaniṣṭhitaḥ bhittiḥ paropajīvitvaṃ parā prajñātha tatkṛtiḥ

plain_english: Whoever truly knows becomes an accomplished yogi and an initiated one.
sanskrit_cite: adṛṣṭamaṇḍalo@pyevaṃ yaḥ kaścidvetti tattvataḥ sa siddhibhāgbhavennityaṃ sa yogī sa ca dīkṣitaḥ

plain_english: Thus, for one who knows by truth, initiation leads to liberation, as declared in that holy treatise.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yo vetti tattvena tasya nirvāṇagāminī dīkṣā bhavediti proktaṃ tacchrītriṃśakaśāsane

plain_english: The unimagined guru is known by knowledge and remembered as innate; one without meditation on that form lacks the supreme.
sanskrit_cite: akalpito gururjñayaḥ sāṃsiddhika iti smṛtaḥ yastu tadrūpabhāgātmabhāvanātaḥ paraṃ vinā

plain_english: A scripture knower is called guru in scripture, declared as an imagined imaginer, and his distinctions arise by superior, medium, and inferior means.
sanskrit_cite: śāstravitsa guruḥ śāstre prokto@kalpitakalpakaḥ tasyāpi bhedā utkṛṣṭamadhyamandādyupāyataḥ

plain_english: From meditation, chanting, dream, vow, or offering, the great-minded one obtains unimagined great initiation.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvanāto@tha vā dhyānājjapātsvapnādvratāddhuteḥ prāpnotyakalpitodāramabhiṣekaṃ mahāmatiḥ

plain_english: This is in the holy Vajasaneya, Vira, and Brahmayamala, and is clearly declared elsewhere by the creator.
sanskrit_cite: śrīmadvājasanīye śrīvīre śrībrahmayāmale śrīsiddhāyāmidaṃ dhātrā proktamanyatra ca sphuṭam

plain_english: Due to self-will, his activity is accepted as infinite, sometimes through devotion yoga, action, or knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tasya svecchāpravṛttatvātkāraṇānantateṣyate kadācidbhaktiyogena karmaṇā vidyayāpi vā

plain_english: By teaching of knowledge and dharma, by mantras, initiation, and many similar means, the supreme lord acts.
sanskrit_cite: jñānadharmopadeśena mantrairvā dīkṣayāpi vā evamādyairanekaiśca prakāraiḥ parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: The lord of the universe graces worldly beings, dear one, through mother-circle awakening and purification.
sanskrit_cite: saṃsāriṇo@nugṛhṇāti viśvasya jagataḥ patiḥ mātṛmaṇḍalasaṃbodhātsaṃskārāttapasaḥ priye

plain_english: From meditation, yoga, chanting, knowledge, mantra worship, and vow, one obtains family-common knowledge that grants kaula accomplishment.
sanskrit_cite: dhyānādyogājjapājjñānānmantrārādhanāto vratāt saṃprāpyaṃ kulasāmānyaṃ jñānaṃ kaulikasiddhidam

plain_english: Wherever the goal consisting of truth-knowledge is seen, he indeed is guru there; let the network of causes be imagined.
sanskrit_cite: tattvajñānātmakaṃ sādhyaṃ yatra yatraiva dṛśyate sa eva hi gurustatra hetujālaṃ prakalpyatām

plain_english: Without truth-knowledge there is no other mark; this is declared in Brahmayamala when service is done without doubt.
sanskrit_cite: tattvajñānādṛte nānyallakṣaṇaṃ brahmayāmale tatraiva coktaṃ sevāyāṃ kṛtāyāmavikalpataḥ

plain_english: If the practitioner has no success, self-initiation is given through the naming sequence.
sanskrit_cite: sādhakasya na cetsiddhiḥ kiṃ kāryamiti codite ātmīyamasya saṃjñānakrameṇa svātmadīkṣaṇam

plain_english: Then self-knowledge, establishing vividness, accomplishes what is to be accomplished.
sanskrit_cite: sasphuratvaprasiddhyarthaṃ tataḥ sādhyaṃ prasiddhyati anena svātmavijñānaṃ sasphuratvaprasādhakam

plain_english: If the primary teacher is not vivid, then again in the worship of red Tara.
sanskrit_cite: uktaṃ mukhyatayācāryo bhavedyadi na sasphuraḥ tatraiva ca punaḥ śrīmadraktārādhanakarmaṇi

plain_english: Doing the declared rule always, the teacher is monthly, the practitioner is half-fortnight initiate, and so on.
sanskrit_cite: vidhiṃ proktaṃ sadā kurvanmāsenācārya ucyate pakṣeṇa sādhako@rdhārdhātputrakaḥ samayī tathā

plain_english: When the teacher is unavailable, one should perform this declared rule by mantra practice of the red goddess from the sequence.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣayejjapayogena raktādevī kramādyataḥ guroralābhe proktasya vidhimetaṃ samācaret

plain_english: In opinion, in study from a book, such a fault is said; if that fault is absent, there is no prohibition.
sanskrit_cite: mate ca pustakādvidyādhyayane doṣa īdṛśaḥ ukto yastena taddoṣābhāve@sau na niṣiddhatā

plain_english: When asked what fruit comes from secrecy of mantra and substances, book-learned knowledge belongs to those devoid of the initiation rite.
sanskrit_cite: mantradravyādiguptatve phalaṃ kimiti codite pustakādhītavidyā ye dīkṣāsamayavarjitāḥ

plain_english: Dark-natured ones practice harm to others and subjugation enough, but they do not know truth; thus they are clearly fault-bearing.
sanskrit_cite: tāmasāḥ parahiṃsādi vaśyādi ca carantyalam na ca tattvaṃ vidustena doṣabhāja iti sphuṭam

plain_english: First a pair of words is to be spoken mutually as cause and effect; but without scripture one does not attain pure-knowledge-named awareness.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvaṃ padayugaṃ vācyamanyonyaṃ hetuhetumat yastu śāstraṃ vinā naiti śuddhavidyākhyasaṃvidam

plain_english: He who seeks the scripture declared by the teacher should perform the sequence, having worshipped the teacher with devotion by any means.
sanskrit_cite: guroḥ sa śāstramanvicchustaduktaṃ kramamācaret yena kenāpyupāyena gurumārādhya bhaktitaḥ

plain_english: By that initiation sequence he knows the meaning of scripture; then, having obtained consecration, he becomes appointed.
sanskrit_cite: taddīkṣākramayogena śāstrārthaṃ vettyasau tataḥ abhiṣekaṃ samāsādya yo bhavetsa tu kalpitaḥ

plain_english: Skilled in removing all bonds, he acts by proper sequence in some scriptural matter.
sanskrit_cite: sannapyaśeṣapāśaughavinivartanakovidaḥ yo yathākramayogena kasmiṃścicchāstravastuni

plain_english: Sudden awakening occurs; among imagined and unimagined parts, the unimagined part is remembered as most excellent.
sanskrit_cite: ākasmikaṃ brajedbodhaṃ kalpitākalpito hi saḥ tasya yo@kalpito bhāgaḥ sa tu śreṣṭhamaḥ smṛtaḥ

plain_english: Excellence arises from degrees of pure knowledge, as difference begins from accomplished Shiva and liberated Shiva is below.
sanskrit_cite: utkarṣaḥ śuddhavidyāṃśatāratamyakṛto yataḥ yathā bhedenādisiddhācchivānmuktaśivā hyadhaḥ

plain_english: Thus lower possessors of acquired knowledge have no authority in its presence, like liberated Shiva self.
sanskrit_cite: tathā sāṃsiddhikajñānādāhṛtajñānino@dhamāḥ tatsaṃnidhau nādhikārasteṣāṃ muktaśivātmavat

plain_english: But silent standing or action remains; following that is duty, and even unimagined form makes agreement firm.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ tu tūṣṇīṃ-sthitiryadvā kṛtyaṃ tadanuvartanam yastvakalpitarūpo@pi saṃvādadṛḍhatākṛte

plain_english: A teacher who obtained impressions elsewhere is directly Bhairava, because of scripture order and practice of that knowing teacher's wisdom.
sanskrit_cite: anyato labdhasaṃskāraḥ sa sākṣādbhairavo guruḥ yataḥ śāstrakramāttajjñaguruprajñānuśīlanāt

plain_english: Self-ascertained knowledge becomes Bhairava through fullness; it is stated from teacher, scripture, and self.
sanskrit_cite: ātmapratyayitaṃ jñānaṃ pūrṇatvādbhairavāyate tena śrīkiraṇoktaṃ yadgurutaḥ śāstrataḥ svataḥ

plain_english: This knowledge has three sources; it shines through aggregate, inversion, and forms in night wandering.
sanskrit_cite: tripratyayamidaṃ jñānamiti yacca niśāṭane tatsaṃghātaviparyāsavigrahairbhāsate tathā

plain_english: Because of variety, instruments take axe, chisel, and saw to perform cutting.
sanskrit_cite: karaṇasya vicitratvādvicitrāmeva tāṃ chidam kartuṃ vāsīṃ ca ṭaṅkaṃ ca krakacaṃ cāpi gṛhṇate

plain_english: Cutting is one from initial intention; thus the instrument's own body is to be spoken in measure.
sanskrit_cite: tāvacca chedanaṃ hyekaṃ tathaivādyābhisaṃdhitaḥ itthameva mitau vācyaṃ karaṇasya svakaṃ vapuḥ

plain_english: Measure is not independent from self; attainment is not by force, and the knower's breath limit is said.
sanskrit_cite: na svatantraṃ svato mānaṃ kuryādadhigamaṃ haṭhāt pramātrāśvāsaparyanto yato@dhigama ucyate

plain_english: Breath is various from power descent; even in measure, measures have clear space.
sanskrit_cite: āśvāsaśca vicitro@sau śaktipātavaśāttathā pramite@pi pramāṇānāmavakāśo@styataḥ sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Having seen, embraced, and chewed long with mind, the beloved satisfies them; what can we say to them?
sanskrit_cite: dṛṣṭvā dṛṣṭvā samāśliṣya ciraṃ saṃcarvya cetasā priyā yaiḥ parituṣyeta kiṃ brūmaḥ kila tānprati

plain_english: Thus even in mental immersion, no path is attained; there is no futility, no infinite regress, and no mutual dependence.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ ca mānasaṃplutyāmapi nādhigate gatiḥ na vyarthatā nānavasthā nānyonyāśrayatāpi ca

plain_english: Thus in yoga-limb inquiry, reasoning alone is not another inner means; it is for excellence of reflection.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yogāṅgamiyati tarka eva na cāparam antarantaḥ parāmarśapāṭavātiśayāya saḥ

plain_english: The five restraints—non-harm, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, non-possession—are not useful in direct awareness.
sanskrit_cite: ahiṃsā satyamasteyabrahmacaryāparigrahāḥ iti pañca yamāḥ sākṣātsaṃvittau nopayoginaḥ

plain_english: Austerities and observances, posture, and breath control—all this is external manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: tapaḥprabhṛtayo ye ca niyamā yattathāsanam prāṇāyāmāśca ye sarvametadbāhyavijṛmbhitam

plain_english: In Viravali it was said: in awareness only, of Shiva-nature, by mind-dissolution bond, moon and sun are dissolved.
